tips: Use USED (already-brewed) coffee grounds, patted dry on a towel, as the exfoliant. Dry, unbrewed grounds can bleed and leave a brown halo of color in the bar. A good starting rate is about 1 teaspoon of grounds per pound of soap, added at trace; increase from there for a scrubbier bar. Grounds are a large, aggressive exfoliant, best for feet, elbows, and gardener bars.

Strong brewed coffee can replace part or all of the water in the lye solution, but chill it completely (cold or even frozen) before adding lye. Like milk and teas, a warm sugary liquid plus lye heat leads to scorching and off odors; any odd scent in fresh coffee soap fades during cure.

Activated charcoal dosing (The Nerdy Farm Wife's tested table, per pound of oils): 1/8 to 1/2 tsp gives light-to-medium gray soap with white lather; 1 tsp gives dark gray soap with a faint gray lather; 2 tsp to 1 tablespoon gives black soap but noticeably gray lather that can temporarily mark washcloths and soap dishes. Stay at or below about 1 tsp PPO if white lather matters.

Cocoa powder: about 1 teaspoon per pound of soap at light trace yields a medium chocolate brown (start at 1/2 tsp PPO and work up). Always sift and pre-disperse it in a little light oil or water because it clumps, and choose Dutch-process cocoa for a darker, richer brown than natural cocoa.
